messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting (freezing) point of pure water drops below the normal 0 °C.  
According to the water phase diagram, the solid–liquid equilibrium line at 10 kPa lies at roughly **–2 °C**.  

So, water would freeze at about **–2 °C** when the ambient pressure is 10 kPa.
